## Keating: TUI, pi framework, Generative UI tools, and E2E testing

### 1. The TUI implementation

Keating has **two separate terminal UIs**, both launched from `src/cli/main.ts` (dispatch at lines ~501–513):

- **`keating shell` → the classic Pi TUI** (`launchShell`). This is the real, full-featured interface. It runs the hyperteacher extension in-process on top of `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` + `@earendil-works/pi-tui`. Interactive tool cards and `ctx.ui.custom` forms work here.
- **`keating tui` → the OpenTUI host** (`src/tui/opentui-host.ts`, `launchOpenTui`). Built on `@opentui/core` (`BoxRenderable`, `InputRenderable`, `ScrollBoxRenderable`, `TextRenderable`, `createCliRenderer`). It is a **thin RPC client** that talks to Pi over RPC (`launchRpcClient` from `src/runtime/pi.ts`).

State of the OpenTUI host: **partial / text-only**. It renders a header, a status line, a scrollable transcript, and an input box. It streams assistant `message_update`/`message_end` events as plain text. Critically, it does **not** render any interactive/generative UI. When an extension issues an `extension_ui_request` with method `select`/`confirm`/`input`/`editor`, it posts a notice ("This extension requested a Pi-specific input surface. Switch with /shell to use it.") and **cancels the request** (`sendUiResponse(id, { cancelled: true })`, opentui-host.ts lines 176–179). Typing `/shell` tears down OpenTUI and hands off to the classic Pi shell.

TUI-side rendering code (used by the classic Pi shell, not OpenTUI):
- `src/pi/hyper-teacher/tui-components.ts` — `renderCard`, `renderArtifactPreview`, `renderQuizCard`, `renderGoalCard`, `renderGoalListCard`, and the interactive `AnswerFormComponent` (keyboard-driven quiz form built from pi-tui `Input`/`SelectList`).
- `src/pi/hyper-teacher/header-component.ts`, `setup-wizard.ts`, `ui-helpers.ts`.

### 2. Generative UI tools — web vs TUI support

Two parallel tool implementations exist:
- **CLI/TUI extension tools:** `src/pi/hyper-teacher/tools/*` registered via `registerKeatingTools` (`tools/index.ts`), built with `keatingToolMaker` in `tools/shared.ts`. Each tool can attach a `renderResult(result, options, theme)` that returns a pi-tui `Component`.
- **Web browser tools:** `web/src/keating/browser-tools/*` (`assessment.ts`, `teaching.ts`, `media.ts`, `improvement.ts`, `workspace.ts`), built with `createTool` (`browser-tools/shared.ts`), returning **strings that embed interactive tags**.

**Web rendering mechanism (per project memory, confirmed):** tools emit a self-closing custom tag with a **double-JSON-encoded** payload: `` `<keating-quiz json=${JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(quiz))} />` `` (e.g. `assessment.ts:177`, `teaching.ts:76/287/338`, `media.ts:298/422`, `AssistantChatPanel.tsx:3569`). `web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx` parses these with regexes (`quizTagPattern`, `sceneTagPattern`, `questionTagPattern`, `goalTagPattern`, `generatedImageTagPattern`, `quizResultTagPattern`, ~lines 1255–1260) and renders React components (`QuizRenderer`, `QuestionRenderer`, `GoalRenderer`, `QuizResultCard`, `FlashcardRenderer`, `MermaidRenderer`, `SceneRenderer`). User interaction dispatches **window CustomEvents** (`keating:quiz-submitted`, `keating:question-answered`, `keating:card-reviewed`, `keating:quiz-remediation-requested`, `keating:quiz-reframe-requested`), which listeners feed back into the agent via **`onNew(...)`** (AssistantChatPanel.tsx ~3350, 3421, 3461, 3570). The **`resultId` feedback loop**: the `quiz` tool stores open-ended answers under a generated `resultId` (`pendingQuizResults`, shared.ts) and instructs the model to call `grade_quiz`/`grade_question_checks` with that id (teaching.ts:126–136 CLI; assessment.ts:210–248 web emits `<keating-quiz-grade …/>`).

Interactive/generative tool inventory and where handled:

| Tool | Web tool (browser-tools) | Web tag / renderer | TUI/CLI tool (hyper-teacher) | TUI render support |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **quiz** | `assessment.ts` "quiz" | `<keating-quiz>` → QuizRenderer | `tools/teaching.ts` "quiz" | Yes — `ctx.ui.custom` → `AnswerFormComponent` (interactive) + `renderQuizCard`; falls back to markdown when no UI |
| **grade_quiz** | `assessment.ts` "grade_quiz" | `<keating-quiz-grade>` / QuizResultCard | `tools/teaching.ts` "grade_quiz" | Yes — `renderQuizCard` with grades |
| **quiz-result** (learner submission) | AssistantChatPanel.tsx:3569 | `<keating-quiz-result>` → QuizResultCard | — | No (web-only feedback tag) |
| **question / ask_user_question** | `assessment.ts` "ask_user_question" | `<keating-question>` → QuestionRenderer | `tools/ask-user-question.ts` | Partial — pi shell `ctx.ui`; OpenTUI cancels it |
| **grade_question_checks** | `assessment.ts` "grade_question_checks" | (question grading) | — | n/a |
| **goal / set_learner_goal / update_goal_step / list_learner_goals** | `teaching.ts` | `<keating-goal>` → GoalRenderer | `tools/goals.ts` | Card-only — `renderGoalCard`/`renderGoalListCard` (non-interactive) |
| **plan** | `assessment.ts` (artifact) | `[artifact://plan/...]` markdown | `tools/teaching.ts` "plan" | Card — `artifactPreviewRenderer("Lesson Plan")` |
| **map** | (concept map) | Mermaid → MermaidRenderer | `tools/teaching.ts` "map" | Card — `artifactPreviewRenderer("Concept Map")` |
| **verify** | — | — | `tools/teaching.ts` "verify" | Card — `artifactPreviewRenderer("Verification Checklist")` |
| **animate** | `media.ts` "animate" | `<keating-animation>` → SceneRenderer | `tools/teaching.ts` "animate" | Card — `artifactPreviewRenderer("Animation Storyboard")` |
| **generate_image** | `media.ts` "generate_image" | `<keating-image>` | — | No (web-only) |
| **deck (flashcards)** | `teaching.ts` "deck" | `<keating-deck>` → FlashcardRenderer | — | No (web-only) |
| **scene** | — | `<keating-scene>` → SceneRenderer | — | No (web-only) |

Bottom line on TUI support: the **classic Pi shell** renders all hyper-teacher tools as bordered cards and supports one genuinely interactive form (quiz via `AnswerFormComponent`). The **OpenTUI host renders none of them** — it explicitly declines every extension UI request. Several generative tools (`generate_image`, `deck`/flashcards, `scene`, `quiz-result`) are **web-only** with no CLI/TUI equivalent.

### 3. The pi framework interface and plugins

pi packages in use (all `@earendil-works`, pinned in `bun.lock`):
- **Root (`package.json`):** `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent ^0.80.2` (locked 0.80.2), `@earendil-works/pi-tui ^0.80.2` (0.80.2). Also `@opentui/core ^0.4.3` and `ink ^7.1.0` (ink is a dependency but the active alternate TUI is OpenTUI, not ink).
- **Web (`web/package.json`):** `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core ^0.80.2`, `@earendil-works/pi-ai ^0.80.2`, `@earendil-works/pi-web-ui ^0.75.3`.
- **No `pi-proxy`** package is present anywhere.

Plugin/extension system: Keating declares itself a pi package (`package.json` `"pi": { "extensions": ["./dist/src/pi"], "skills": ["./pi/skills"], "prompts": ["./pi/prompts"] }`). The extension entry is `src/pi/hyper-teacher/index.ts` — `export default function hyperteacher(pi)` which calls `pi.registerCommand(...)` (plan, map, animate, bench, evolve, prompt-evolve, setup, packages, verify, feedback, improve, outputs, speech, policy, version, …) and `registerKeatingTools(pi)` / `registerSpeechTool(pi)`. Tools use `pi.registerTool` (guarded by a `WeakSet` to avoid double registration). The extension talks to the UI through `ctx.ui` (`setEditorText`, `select`, `custom`, `notify`, `setStatus`) and stores the active context via `setActiveCtx` (shared.ts). The web app does not load the pi extension; it re-implements the tools as browser tools and drives the agent via `useKeatingAgent` (`web/src/hooks/useKeatingAgent.tsx`) using `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` `Agent`, `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, and `defaultConvertToLlm` from `@earendil-works/pi-web-ui`.

**Gaps where the OpenTUI host lags web/classic shell:** no interactive cards, no `select`/`confirm`/`input`/`editor` surfaces (cancelled outright), no quiz/goal/question/flashcard/image/scene rendering, no `resultId` feedback loop UI — it only streams text and offers `/shell` as an escape hatch.

### 4. Testing harness and API keys

- Tests run with **`bun test`**: root suite `bun test ./test/*.test.ts` (justfile `test`), web suite `cd web && bun test` (justfile `test-web`). Web has two dirs: `web/src/test/*.test.ts` (~65 files) and `web/test/*.test.ts`. Strategy doc: `docs/TESTING.md` (Antithesis-style "system laws", property/fuzz tests via `fast-check`; also Stryker mutation testing via `stryker.config.json`).
- **How e2e tests obtain API keys:** environment variables, gated with early-return guards — **not** a secret manager. The real-model tests use Gemini by default: `test/fuzz.test.ts:16`, `test/evolution.test.ts:168/189`, `test/map-elites.test.ts:279` all do `if (!process.env.GOOGLE_API_KEY && !process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY) return;` (silently skip when no key). `test/package.test.ts` exercises env plumbing for `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ZYPHRA_API_KEY`. No test hardcodes or fetches a live key.

Provider auth/env handling lives in `src/core/provider-auth.ts` (`PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS`, `envWithProviderAliases`) — env-var based.
- **minimax / minimax-m2.7-highspeed:** **not found.** No `minimax-m2.7-highspeed` anywhere. My strongest impression is that Keating has the right pieces, but several interfaces currently look unified to the learner while remaining separate systems internally. That creates subtle consistency and safety risks.

The most important things I’d think about next:

1. Voice is not yet a first-class conversation record

The Realtime session now uses Keating’s tools, but it remains a separate model connection. User speech is copied into the composer when the session ends, while assistant speech, tool calls, citations, and intermediate turns are not fully persisted into the main Pi session.

That can cause:

- Voice and text having different memories.
- Learning analytics seeing only part of the lesson.
- A goal or quiz changing state without a durable explanation of why.
- Session recovery losing the spoken exchange.

I would create one canonical event log shared by text, voice, TUI, and web. Realtime events should become ordinary Keating messages and tool-result records as they happen.

2. Voice currently receives a very powerful tool catalog

The bridge exposes the active browser/Pi tools directly to the Realtime model. That is powerful, but spoken instructions can now trigger state-changing tools with less visible review than typed chat.

I’d classify tools:

- Safe and automatic: search, read learner context, list goals.
- Confirm before execution: update goals, grade work, change persistent state.
- Never available to voice without explicit enablement: filesystem, shell, provider configuration, destructive operations.

Confirmation should happen in the visible overlay before the function result is returned.

3. Live voice still lacks a clean web-search contract

Provider-native search is correctly injected into ordinary Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic chat requests. But OpenAI Realtime does not automatically inherit the main chat model’s hosted search tool. It only sees Keating’s function catalog—and there currently isn’t a unified `web_search` function guaranteed to be in that catalog.

So “voice has tools” does not necessarily mean “voice can search.”

I’d introduce one Keating `web_search` capability that:

- Uses the active provider’s hosted search when available.
- Falls back to a configured search provider.
- Returns normalized citations.
- Works identically in voice, web chat, classic Pi, and OpenTUI.
- Records query, sources, provider, and retrieval time.

4. Search quality needs more than enabling provider tools

The current `webSearch: auto` behavior effectively makes hosted search available on eligible requests and lets the model decide. I’d add explicit retrieval policy:

- Search required for current events, prices, laws, product details, medicine, and recent research.
- Search optional for stable concepts.
- Require citations for factual claims derived from search.
- Show source freshness and provider.
- Detect answers that searched but omitted citations.
- Evaluate source diversity and primary-source preference.

The regex-based provider capability detection will also drift as models are released. A provider capability registry would be safer than model-name pattern matching.

5. Generative UI is still implemented three times

There are effectively separate rendering systems:

- React/custom tags in the web app.
- Pi components in the classic shell.
- Plain terminal cards in OpenTUI.

The similarity check caught one direct symptom: `goalCardLines` and `renderGoalCard`. The larger issue is semantic drift. A quiz may support feedback, remediation, and reframe actions on the web but only sequential questions in OpenTUI.

I’d define shared, serializable UI documents:

```ts
{
  kind: "quiz",
  version: 1,
  data: { ... },
  actions: [...]
}
```

Each host would render that document. Tools would stop returning host-specific HTML-like tags or Pi components. This would also make plugins considerably easier to support.

6. OpenTUI’s interaction model is functional but not equivalent yet

The new standard dialogs prevent crashes, but complex Pi `custom()` components cannot cross RPC. Classification worksheets, matching, rich quiz navigation, images, flashcards, and scenes still lose fidelity.

Longer-term options:

- Extend Pi RPC with a serializable custom-view protocol.
- Build the shared UI-document protocol above.
- Keep classic Pi as the explicitly richer terminal interface.

I would avoid pretending the two TUI modes have parity until this is resolved.

7. The E2E harness needs stronger semantic assertions

The MiniMax harness proves:

- Skate secret resolution.
- Custom provider configuration.
- Embedded Pi startup.
- Extension command discovery.
- Real model requests and tool calling.

But it currently asserts a built-in `read` call, not a full Keating quiz → UI response → grading cycle. During investigation, MiniMax ignored the requested quiz tool and used filesystem tools to locate the implementation. That is valuable evidence.

A stronger harness should restrict available tools and assert:

- `quiz` is visible to the model.
- An RPC dialog is emitted.
- The host answers it.
- `grade_quiz` follows where required.
- A generative card is produced.
- Learner state changes exactly once.

8. Tool results need size, privacy, and display boundaries

Realtime function outputs currently return raw tool results to the model. Some results may contain large artifacts, internal paths, learner records, or custom UI tags.

I’d add a normalization layer that:

- Separates model-visible output from UI-visible details.
- Truncates large results.
- Redacts secrets and private metadata.
- Stores artifacts by reference.
- Preserves citations and structured UI payloads separately.

9. Direct WebRTC is probably the right default—but clarify the boundary

I agree with keeping direct OpenAI WebRTC for the current single-learner product. LiveKit becomes compelling if you need:

- Multiple participants.
- Teacher/observer handoff.
- SIP or telephone integration.
- Server-side recording.
- Regional media routing.
- Centralized quality and latency telemetry.
- Provider switching without reconnecting the browser.

I’d hide transport behind a `DuplexSessionTransport` now, so LiveKit can be added later without rewriting the voice interface.

10. Observability should follow the learner experience

You’ll want metrics beyond request latency:

- Time to first audio.
- Interruption success rate.
- False VAD turn rate.
- Tool-call latency during speech.
- Search-to-citation rate.
- Voice session reconnection rate.
- Quiz abandonment by interface.
- Whether spoken sessions improve later retrieval.

A voice interaction can feel bad despite every API call technically succeeding.

11. Release state currently has two competing truths

The release attempt exposed a notable workflow issue: Bumpy already held a pending 2.5.0 minor entry while `package.json` remained the canonical 2.4.0 source. Running Bumpy consumed the pending entry, while version synchronization pulled in the opposite direction.

That should be resolved before the next release:

- Decide whether Bumpy or root `package.json` owns version intent.
- Prevent `sync-version` from fighting pending Bumpy releases.
- Add a dry-run release command showing exactly what will be consumed.

My priority order would be:

1. Canonical cross-interface event log.
2. Voice tool permissions and confirmations.
3. Unified search capability with citation normalization.
4. Shared generative-UI document protocol.
5. Semantic voice/quiz E2E coverage.
6. Transport abstraction and observability.
7. Consolidate deterministic browser/core duplication.

The application’s opportunity is bigger than “chat with voice.” Keating can become a continuous learning environment where every interface—voice, text, terminal, artifacts, and plugins—participates in the same durable lesson. The main remaining work is making that conceptual unity true in the architecture.

Execution plan created and sequenced around architectural dependencies.

### Release 1 — Unified foundation

1. Canonical event log

   Define versioned events for text, voice, tool calls, citations, interruptions, UI documents, and learner-state mutations.

   Done when sessions can be persisted, replayed, recovered, and rendered consistently across interfaces.

2. Capability and permission layer

   Classify tools as automatic, confirmation-required, or restricted. Route voice and text execution through the same enforcement point.

   Done when spoken instructions cannot silently trigger sensitive mutations.

### Release 2 — Search and generative UI

3. Unified `web_search`

   Build provider adapters for Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic hosted search, with fallback support, normalized citations, freshness rules, and source metadata.

   Done when the same search contract works through web chat, voice, Pi shell, and OpenTUI.

4. Serializable generative UI

   Replace custom web tags, Pi-specific components, and plain-card result logic with versioned UI documents rendered by host adapters.

   Initial document types:

   - Quiz and grading
   - Questions, matching, and classification
   - Goals
   - Search results
   - Artifacts
   - Flashcards
   - Images and scenes

   Done when tools produce one semantic result regardless of interface.

### Release 3 — Truly unified voice

5. Persist Realtime activity continuously

   Record user and assistant transcripts, interruptions, tool calls, search citations, UI documents, and resulting state changes as they happen.

   Done when switching from voice to text preserves the complete conversation and learning state.

6. Harden Realtime execution

   Add confirmation UI, output normalization, size limits, secret redaction, reconnect handling, and tool-result references.

   Done when voice can safely use every permitted Keating capability without bypassing application controls.

### Release 4 — OpenTUI parity and proof

7. Complete OpenTUI workflows

   Add updateable widgets, richer quizzes, matching/classification forms, artifact references, media cards, cancellation, and reconnect behavior.

8. Semantic E2E harness

   Cover:

   - Voice → search → cited answer
   - Voice → quiz → answers → grading
   - Confirmation-required tool calls
   - Generative UI rendering in every host
   - Session persistence and recovery
   - Provider fallback behavior
   - Learner-state mutation exactly once

   Use deterministic provider fixtures in CI and opt-in MiniMax/OpenAI live tests.

### Release 5 — Production hardening

9. Transport and observability

   Introduce a `DuplexSessionTransport` abstraction while retaining direct WebRTC. Track first-audio latency, VAD errors, interruptions, tool latency, citation rates, reconnects, and learning outcomes.

   Adopt LiveKit only when multi-party sessions, SIP, centralized recording, regional routing, or server-mediated provider switching becomes necessary.

10. Consolidation and release workflow

   - Share high-value browser/core logic.
   - Add an allowlist for intentional browser ports.
   - Make new similarity findings release-blocking.
   - Establish one version authority between Bumpy and `sync-version`.
   - Add a release dry-run showing consumed bump entries and resulting versions.

Recommended first implementation slice: canonical events, tool permissions, and unified search. Those three unlock safe voice integration and prevent the UI work from being built on another temporary contract.
